script.text: Permanent Daylight Saving Time would improve road and travel safety on balance.
script.label: Add mixed road-safety evidence

script.text: Permanent Daylight Saving Time may reduce overall fatal crashes by aligning daylight with higher-traffic evening periods.
script.label: Add the overall road-safety claim

script.text: Year-round Daylight Saving Time could reduce pedestrian fatalities by shifting daylight to busier evening travel periods.
script.label: Add pedestrian safety

script.text: Shifting daylight later can reduce bicyclist fatal crashes.
script.label: Add bicyclist safety

script.text: Year-round Daylight Saving Time could reduce motor-vehicle occupant fatalities.
script.label: Add occupant safety

script.text: Recent U.S. data suggest that shifting daylight later can increase motor-vehicle occupant fatal crashes.
script.label: Rebut occupant safety

script.text: A systematic review found the road-safety evidence insufficient to support or refute a net benefit from permanently shifting daylight later.
script.label: Add the road-safety review

script.text: A large contemporary study found no significant increase in acute myocardial infarction during daylight-saving-time transition weeks.
script.label: Rebut cardiovascular events

script.text: A large English cohort study found little evidence that the spring clock change increases several acute mental and physical health events.
script.label: Rebut acute health effects

script.text: An Ontario worker-compensation study found no increase in work-injury claims immediately after the spring clock change.
script.label: Rebut workplace injuries

script.text: Permanent Daylight Saving Time would worsen circadian alignment and sleep on balance.
script.label: Add circadian alignment and sleep

script.text: Permanent Standard Time aligns better with human circadian biology than permanent Daylight Saving Time.
script.label: Add permanent Standard Time alignment

script.text: A broad set of medical, sleep, safety, and parent organizations endorse permanent Standard Time rather than permanent Daylight Saving Time.
script.label: Add medical consensus

script.text: A recent circadian model projected that either permanent clock would reduce circadian burden compared with biannual switching.
script.label: Add the circadian model

script.text: The same model projected better health outcomes under permanent Standard Time than under permanent Daylight Saving Time.
script.label: Add the model's Standard Time result

script.text: Methodological criticism challenges the recent U.S. circadian-health model.
script.label: Challenge the circadian model

script.text: The Sunshine Protection Act would create net implementation, coordination, and legal-flexibility costs.
script.label: Add implementation costs

script.text: A permanent U.S. time-policy change could disrupt airline schedules, passenger travel, and international coordination.
script.label: Add airline coordination

script.text: A patchwork of neighboring jurisdictions with different clock observances can create scheduling and travel complexity.
script.label: Add jurisdictional complexity

script.text: The Sunshine Protection Act would reduce future jurisdictional flexibility over time policy on balance.
script.label: Add reduced state flexibility

script.text: States may lose the ability to choose permanent Standard Time without another federal-law change.
script.label: Add the state-choice restriction

script.text: Permanent Daylight Saving Time would be broadly acceptable to the public on balance.
script.label: Add public acceptance

script.text: Historical experiences with permanent Daylight Saving Time or permanent summer time are unfavorable on balance.
script.label: Add unfavorable historical evidence

script.text: The 1974 U.S. year-round Daylight Saving Time experiment became unpopular largely because of dark winter mornings.
script.label: Add the 1974 U.S. experience

script.text: The 1974 U.S. experience may be a weaker guide today because school and commuting patterns have changed.
script.label: Qualify the historical evidence

script.text: Russia adopted permanent summer time in 2011 and reversed it in 2014 after the policy became widely unpopular.
script.label: Add the Russian experience

script.text: Support for permanent Daylight Saving Time is broadly distributed across populations and jurisdictions.
script.label: Add distributed public support

script.text: Nineteen states have enacted laws or trigger provisions supporting year-round Daylight Saving Time if federal law permits it.
script.label: Add state support

script.text: A 2025 three-choice poll preferred permanent Standard Time over permanent Daylight Saving Time.
script.label: Rebut public acceptance
